title: Product stable-influence estimate
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let $P$ be a finite product probability space with $n$ coordinates, and let $\lambda,q,\rho\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfy $0<\lambda$, $\lambda\le 1$, $q\ge 2$, $\rho\ge 0$, and $\rho\le \frac{1}{q-1}\lambda^{1-2/q}$. Suppose every coordinate atom has probability at least $\lambda$. For every function $f$ taking values in $\{-1,1\}$ and every coordinate $i$, $\rho I_i^{(\rho)}(f)\le I_i(f)^{2-2/q}$.
hypotheses_covered: $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and a finite product probability space $P$ with $n$ coordinates
Every coordinate atom has probability at least $\lambda$
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ with every coordinate atom at least $0<\lambda\le1$, and let $q\ge2$ and $0\le\rho\le\lambda^{1-2/q}/(q-1)$. For every $f:\Omega\to\{-1,1\}$ and coordinate $i$, $\rho I_i^{(\rho)}(f)\le I_i(f)^{2-2/q}$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $I_i(h)=\mathbb E_P(h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h)^2$; $I_i^{(a)}(h)=\sum_{S\ni i}a^{|S|-1}\mathbb E_Ph_S^2$ for $a\in\mathbb R$. The powers indexed by subset cardinalities are natural powers, including $0^0=1$.
